r.d: Anti-Bullying Week 2026 runs from Monday 16 to Friday 20 November, and the Alliance’s theme is Break the Silence. An assembly on the Monday launches Odd Socks Day, and four themed lunchtimes carry the rest of the week. Each needs one member of staff and forty minutes, and each day stands alone. It is a week about noticing who is on their own.
r.f: 16 to 20 November 2026 · assembly and form time · free to download The Pastoral Guide is a registered supporter of Anti-Bullying Week 2026 .

r.d: A Valentine’s Day fundraiser. Students buy a bag of hot chocolate at break and write an anonymous note to somebody in the school there and then. An adult reads every note, and the bags are delivered on the fourteenth. Slides, a printable pack and a tracker spreadsheet for the orders. It gets students thinking about who might need a good morning.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · assembly or form time · free to download

r.d: Every awareness day and week worth marking in a secondary school year, from September to July, including the United Nations days that lend themselves to an assembly. Each one has the date, one line on what to do with it, and the value it gets students thinking about. Where the site has a resource for the day, it is linked. There is a printable version for the staffroom wall, one page per term.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · assembly or form time · free to download

r.t: World Mental Health Day: An Assembly, a Week and a Lesson
r.d: World Mental Health Day falls on Saturday 10 October in 2026, so the assembly is written for the Friday before. It ends by telling students what is happening the following week. That week runs as five themed lunchtimes, one for each of the Five Ways to Wellbeing, or as a wall of anonymous cards. A PSHE lesson comes with it, on what to say when a friend is struggling.
r.f: 10 October · assembly, lunchtimes and a PSHE lesson · free to download

r.d: Eight ready-made certificates, one for each of the values used across the site, so the right one is always to hand when a student earns it. One printable pack, printed once and kept in a drawer.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: Two title banners, six section headers, cards to write on, name tags and bunting. One pack and an afternoon to cut out and put up, and you supply the board and backing paper. A board with the form’s name and their own work on it is the quickest way to make a room feel like theirs.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · print, cut and put up · free to download

r.d: A board header, a stack of slips and a routine that takes two minutes on a Friday. Anybody can fill in a slip saying what somebody else did that week, and the slips stay up until the next lot. Print it once, cut the slips up, and it runs itself after the first fortnight. It is appreciation rather than reward. Nothing here is earned by coming top of anything.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: A printable postcard for passing on a bit of praise. A teacher can give one to a student, or a student can send one to a teacher or to a friend. You circle who it is for. One pack, printed and cut once, and a minute to write one. It gets people saying thank you out loud.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: Eight A4 posters, one for each value used across the site, each with a plain definition and three examples from a form room. Print the ones you want and put them up. Ten minutes, and nothing else to prepare. Once the words are on the wall, praise and correction can point at something everybody already recognises.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: A week of ten-minute morning activities on questioning what you read. Each day, a newspaper front page shows a claim that was once reported as true. The form argues about it, works out what the evidence shows, then sees the verdict and the one question that would have caught it. Five stories, from sugar to leaded petrol, with four slides each and nothing to print.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 , and it works in Year 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: A goal-setting sheet, started in the first week of a half term and finished in the last. Students write one thing they want to be true by half term and the three things it depends on, then look back at it seven weeks later. Two five-minute registrations, one double-sided sheet each, and nothing to prepare. It builds follow-through rather than ambition.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Every student writes one honest, anonymous compliment for someone else in the form, then finds out what was written about them the next day. Five minutes over two mornings, with slides and a printable pack. It is a simple way of getting students to notice something good in someone else and say so.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Read out a strange-sounding fact. The class votes true or false, then finds out. Five minutes and nothing to prepare, with a deck of ten facts and a printable pack holding ten more. It gets students curious, and used to asking whether something is actually true rather than taking it as read.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.t: Questions for Open Evenings and Open Days
r.d: Five registrations in the weeks before an open evening or a university open day, each with a different kind of question to ask when you get there. Five minutes a morning, with two slide sets, one for Year 10 and 11 and one for Year 12 and 13. Each student takes a sheet of questions with them, so they arrive knowing what to ask.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 , a set each for Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Students notice one thing they’re proud of and add it to a board that keeps growing all year. Five to ten minutes, next to no setup, with slides and a printable pack for the board itself. It gets a form used to noticing their own progress instead of waiting for somebody else to point it out.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: A ten-question quiz played in small teams, with a printed answer sheet for each team. Six questions are on a theme and four are general knowledge, then teams swap sheets and mark each other’s as the answers go up. It takes about fifteen minutes, and the only printing is one sheet per team. Each key stage has its own theme, so students come away knowing something useful as well as their score.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, a quiz each for Year 7 to 9 , Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.t: The Form Time Quiz: Christmas Edition
r.d: A ten-question Christmas quiz played in small teams, with a printed answer sheet for each team. The questions are about Christmas traditions around the world and where they came from: four are fact or myth, then three are multiple choice and three are written answers. Teams swap sheets and mark each other’s as the answers go up. It takes about fifteen minutes, and the only printing is one sheet per team.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, a quiz each for Year 7 to 9 , Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Five short registrations for a form’s last week together, one a morning. They ask for something you are taking with you, a person you want to thank, and a last word to the form. Five minutes a morning, with slides and a sheet of cards each, read out on the last day. It gives a form a proper ending rather than just the bell going.
r.f: Year 11 and 13, and any form’s last week · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: A statement goes on the board, and everyone stands somewhere on a line between agree and disagree. Two or three of them then say why they chose that spot. Five minutes a time, with three slide sets, one per key stage, and a printable pack. It gets a form used to disagreeing out loud, and to changing their mind when somebody makes a better point.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, a set each for Year 7 to 9 , Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Everything a form time reading slot needs when nobody gave you a plan. It has a bookmark of six things to think about whatever you are reading, a log for the wall, and five ways to run the twenty minutes. One printable pack, printed once, and it lasts the year. It builds focus, which is often harder than the reading itself.
r.f: Year 7 to 11 · form time reading · free to download

r.d: One question on the board, and when you call a student’s name they answer it instead of saying “here”. It takes about as long as the register already takes, and it gets every student used to saying something out loud in front of the room. Volume One has ten questions to start with, as slides and a printable pack.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Students pair up, ask each other one question from a card, and listen properly for a full minute before swapping. Five minutes, with one set of cards to print and cut once. It gets them curious about the people they sit next to every day, and better at listening rather than waiting for their turn to talk.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: A short story told in five weekly chapters, five minutes each. Every chapter ends on a choice with no clean answer. The form argues about what the character should do, and the next week reveals what they actually did. It is about doing the right thing when nobody is watching. Five chapters to start with, as slides and a printable pack.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Each morning a prompt beginning “Today I will…” goes on the board, and students finish it out loud with something they can do by home time. You note two or three names and ask them the next morning how it went. About four minutes, with ten prompts to start with as slides and a printable pack. Being asked afterwards is what turns saying it into doing it.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: One big question with no right answer. Put it up, give the room a minute of quiet, then see where the discussion goes. It gets students thinking for themselves, and used to hearing a view they don’t share without needing to win. Three slide sets, one for each key stage, with five questions each.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, a set each for Year 7 to 9 , Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Three short sessions spread across a term on what screen time does to the brain, sleep and concentration, each claim with its own citation. Alongside them you keep a weekly tracker of the whole form’s screen time, and the term ends with two awards from it. Slides, printable worksheets, certificates and the tracker spreadsheet. Students see a pattern in their own behaviour and decide for themselves what to change.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · form time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: A seven-week plan for a new form in September, bringing in one new routine a week rather than thirty rules on the first morning. It gives you the order to do things in, one printing list, and the five routines that should run without you by half term. There are three separate four-page packs: Year 7 to 9, Year 10 and 11, and sixth form.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · a half term · free to download

r.d: Grow a herb from seed as a pair, look after it together for six weeks, then cook with it at home. Six weeks of form time, with slides, a printable pack and a tracker spreadsheet. A hands-on way to build responsibility and care, and my own form loved it.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Student-led lessons for tutor time. A student who loves something teaches the form about it: why they love it, some background, and activities they design themselves. They sign up on a shared spreadsheet, show you their plan the week before, and teach for twenty minutes in Year 7, up to an hour in the sixth form. Nobody has to do one, and you can run them once a month or once a half term. The student teaching gains real confidence, and the rest of the form learns about something they would never have picked.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · once a month or once a half term · free to download

r.d: Students choose a role model, name two values that person shows, then act on those values themselves for a week. It closes with each student giving a two-minute presentation to the form. A week of form time, with slides, a printable project planner and a tracker spreadsheet. It is about living a value for a week rather than naming one in a lesson.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: A lesson for the week mock results come back. Students learn to tell the facts of a result from the story they tell themselves about it. They sort eight cards into facts and stories, then write their own result as one fact and one first move. An hour, with cards for each table and a sheet each.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Most students who watch unkindness do not think they are part of it. In this hour they take one corridor moment and count everyone involved, learn the five roles people play, and write what they would actually say to step in. An hour, with slides and a printable pack.
r.f: Year 7 to 11 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Three one-hour lessons on what makes a snack that lasts until lunch. Students learn the science, make a snack, then design their own. Three slide decks and a printable pack. Part of Healthy Body, Healthy Mind.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: “It was just a joke” is what people say when banter lands badly, and it usually shuts the conversation down. Students sort six everyday moments into joke, not a joke, or cannot tell, then work out what makes the difference. An hour, with slides and a printable pack. They leave with four questions for telling banter from bullying.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Most students think you start something once you feel like it. This lesson shows them it works the other way round. Each of them picks something they have been avoiding, shrinks it down, and does five minutes of it in silence. An hour, with slides and a printable pack. What they take away is the confidence to start before they feel ready.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best from Year 10 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Three one-hour lessons on what five minutes of movement does for your mood and focus. Students predict it, measure it on themselves, then plan four weeks of it. Three slide decks and a printable pack. It builds resilience: doing the small thing even on a bad day. Part of Healthy Body, Healthy Mind.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Groups take a job, plan a month on one wage, then deal with ten things nobody planned for. An hour, with slides and a printable pack. It teaches students to look at the whole month before they spend any of it.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best from Year 10 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Five lessons on questioning what you read, each built around a claim that was printed as true and later fell apart. Students show how much they believe the claim, work through four rounds of evidence, then write the front page the paper should have printed. Each lesson takes 45 minutes to an hour, and they can be taught in any order.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 , and it works in Year 9 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Each student plans one real week of revision on a sheet. Then the slides throw three problems at the plan: a late night, a lost evening and a friend who needs them. Students repair the plan each time. It takes an hour and one sheet per student, and they leave with a plan built for the week they will actually have.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Everyone says sorry, but hardly anyone is taught how. In this hour students sort real apologies from the ones that only sound like it, then learn the four parts of a proper one. They rewrite a bad apology in pairs and mark somebody else’s. Slides and a printable pack. It is an hour about owning what you did rather than explaining it away.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: The UCAS personal statement changed for 2026 entry. One piece of writing became three questions in three boxes, sharing the same 4,000 characters. This resource uses five tutor times to get a first draft of all three answers from every student. There is a page to write each answer on, and a check sheet with a column for the student, a friend and you.
r.f: Year 12 and 13 · five tutor times · free to download

r.d: A one page revision timetable for a single week, with a spare slot already printed on every day. Students plan two sessions a day at most and leave the spares empty, so a missed session moves into a spare instead of wrecking the week. One sheet each, on paper or as a spreadsheet, and nothing to prepare. It teaches students to keep going when a week goes wrong, rather than give up on the plan.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · form time, or at home on a Sunday · free to download

r.d: Small cards for the ten minutes before an exam: things to say to yourself, and things to say to a friend who is panicking in the corridor. There is also a slip for a friend who needs an adult. It takes fifteen minutes of tutor time, then the cards go in a pocket, so students have the words ready before they need them.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · tutor time, then the corridor · free to download

r.d: A spreadsheet with every student down the side and the six half terms across the top. You can see at a glance who you have spoken to properly, and who has gone most of a year without it. Tell it which half term you are in and everyone you have not seen yet turns amber. It catches the students who never cause trouble and never ask for help.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A shuffled deck of prompts for a one-to-one or small-group check-in. A student picks a card at random, and you talk about whatever it asks. About ten minutes, and twenty-four cards to print and cut once. There is no script beyond that, and no answer is wrong. Over time, students get used to talking to you.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A simple printable scale for a check-in when words don’t come easily. A student points to the number that feels closest to today, and that is where the conversation starts. One sheet, and a couple of minutes at the start of a one to one. It helps them put a name to how they are feeling.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: Three printable menus of small resets a student can choose from when they need one. Each is a single sheet, meant to be kept in a pencil case rather than used once and thrown away. Five minutes to talk one through, and then it is theirs. It makes self-care something small and practical that the student chooses.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A printed slip a student posts in a box when they want to talk but cannot say so in front of the form. They write their name, tick how soon, and say as much or as little as they like. One page of slips to print, and a box you supply. Some students will never come and find you. A slip and a box give them a way of asking that costs nothing.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A guide for the tutor to the five minutes of a one-to-one check-in. It covers how to start, what to do with a silence, and when to pass something on. Five pages to print once, including eight better things to say than the phrases everybody reaches for. It is the guidance nobody gives a new form tutor.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one · free to download

r.d: A student sits down with you after something has gone wrong and works out what happened, who it affected, and what they will say next. Ten minutes, one sheet each, and a page of guidance for you. It is not a punishment exercise. It asks for accountability, which is a different thing from being sorry.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one · free to download
